Our Story

At a Glance:
Founded: April 3, 2025

- 17,803 lbs Recovered & Redistributed in Year 1
- 23 Hotel & Ski Resort Partners
- 28 Nonprofit & Community Recipients
- Serving Colorado Communities

Slopes to Hope was founded by Drew Roberts after working in Summit County's hospitality industry and seeing firsthand how much usable winter clothing was being left behind each ski season.

How It Started

While working at the Grand Lodge on Peak 7, I saw firsthand how much winter clothing guests left behind each ski season. For years, these items were donated to the local FIRC thrift stores until those stores closed. When I heard about this at our Rotary Club meeting, I started thinking about all the clothing that would no longer have a place to go.

One question kept coming to mind:

"What are we going to do with all these clothes?"

I reached out to local nonprofits, but none could use that volume of clothing. Through Rotary, I was connected with Christ's Body Ministries in Denver, a homeless shelter that could put the clothing to use helping people in need. I then approached several hotels and resorts in Summit County with a simple proposal:

"Instead of throwing these items away, let me pick them up and deliver them to this shelter in Denver that can get them directly to people in need."

Six hotels agreed.

During the 2023–2024 ski season, we recovered and distributed 3,052 pounds of winter clothing to Christ's Body Ministries. Seeing the impact of those donations showed there was an opportunity to expand the program.

It also raised another question:

"What if more hotels participated?"

Slopes to Hope was created to answer that question and officially became a Colorado nonprofit on April 3, 2025.

Where We Are Today

As of September 2026, 23 hotels and ski resorts throughout Summit County have partnered with Slopes to Hope. During our first full year as a nonprofit, we recovered and redistributed 17,803 pounds of clothing, blankets, linens, and other useful items.

Those donations have been distributed to 28 nonprofit and community organizations serving Summit County, the Denver Metro Area, and Colorado Springs.

What started with one question has become a growing network of hotel partners, volunteers, donors, and nonprofit organizations working together to reduce waste and help people across Colorado.

This is what Slopes to Hope is about:

Reducing Waste and Fostering Hope.


"I believe there is a strong will among the people of this world to help those in need. And if they are given the opportunity and resources, I believe they will."

- DREW ROBERTS, FOUNDER

Recovering More Than Clothing — Restoring Hope

Slopes to Hope is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization based in Breckenridge, Colorado. We partner with local hotels and ski resorts to recover clothing items lost or left behind by guests and visitors, diverting thousands of pounds of waste from Colorado landfills.

These high-quality clothing items are then distributed to homeless shelters, churches, schools, and nonprofits across Summit County, the Denver Metro Area, and Colorado Springs—getting essential gear into the hands of Coloradans facing economic and housing hardships.

Mission

Our mission is to reduce environmental waste and support Coloradans experiencing homelessness and hardship by collecting and repurposing clothing items lost or left behind at hotels and ski resorts.

We distribute these clothes to our nonprofit partners, homeless shelters, schools, and community organizations in Summit County, the Denver Metro Area, and Colorado Springs—diverting thousands of pounds of clothing from Colorado landfills and fostering a more sustainable and compassionate Colorado community.

Why?

Tens of thousands of pounds of winter clothes are left behind or lost by guests at Colorado ski resorts and hotels every year. Most of these clothes end up in our landfills.

There are also tens of thousands of people in Colorado who are experiencing homelessness, or cannot afford proper winter clothing.

We address these two problems with one solution.

How?

We go to the hotels and resorts in Summit County and collect these winter clothes, and then distribute them to homeless shelters, churches, and community organizations. This keeps thousands of pounds of clothes out of the landfill and gets them to the people who need them the most.

How Is It Funded?

We are seeking funding from grants, sponsorships, and individual donors.

We are also exploring different fundraising events, such as an auction for new ski equipment and apparel, or nights at participating resorts. Individuals and businesses may also pledge a penny per pound of clothing we collect and distribute.

How Can You Help?

Beyond donations, we seek help with community outreach and connecting with hotel and resort managers!

We are also seeking volunteers to help us collect clothes from hotels and resorts and deliver them to shelters and nonprofit organizations throughout Colorado.

Contact us!

Effective September 11, 2026

This policy explains how information is handled when you visit the Slopes to Hope website or use services linked or embedded here.

Information you choose to provide

The newsletter signup and contact forms are provided by HubSpot. When you submit a form, the information you enter is sent to HubSpot for Slopes to Hope so the organization can manage subscriptions, respond to messages, and maintain related records. The fields shown on each form determine what information is requested.

Donation and fundraising links take you to third-party services, including Givebutter, RallyUp, and Colorado Gives. Those providers collect and process the information needed for their services under their own terms and privacy policies. Slopes to Hope does not collect payment-card details through this website.

Analytics and cookies

With your permission, this website loads Google Analytics through Google tag GT-MKTP8299 (measurement ID G-XEWDW3TYVZ) to understand site usage. Analytics is not loaded until you accept analytics in the consent interface. You may decline analytics or change your choice at any time using “Cookie settings” in the footer.

Your consent choice is stored in your browser's local storage. Embedded forms and third-party content may use their own cookies or similar technologies when they load or when you interact with them.

Hosting and third-party content

The site is hosted using GitHub Pages. Hosting and network providers may process routine technical information, such as IP addresses, request details, browser information, timestamps, and security logs, to deliver and protect the site.

The site also links to or embeds services such as Google Maps, Instagram, Facebook, and other third-party websites. Those services receive information according to their own practices when their content loads or when you follow a link.

Choices and contact

You can decline optional analytics, change your analytics choice through the footer, avoid submitting forms, and choose whether to visit third-party services. Newsletter messages should provide the applicable subscription-management options.

For questions about this policy or information submitted to Slopes to Hope, email drew@slopestohope.com or use the contact page.

Privacy Policy

Effective September 11, 2026

This policy explains how information is handled when you visit the Slopes to Hope website or use services linked or embedded here.

Information you choose to provide

The newsletter signup and contact forms are provided by HubSpot. When you submit a form, the information you enter is sent to HubSpot for Slopes to Hope so the organization can manage subscriptions, respond to messages, and maintain related records. The fields shown on each form determine what information is requested.

Donation and fundraising links take you to third-party services, including Givebutter, RallyUp, and Colorado Gives. Those providers collect and process the information needed for their services under their own terms and privacy policies. Slopes to Hope does not collect payment-card details through this website.

Analytics and cookies

With your permission, this website loads Google Analytics through Google tag GT-MKTP8299 (measurement ID G-XEWDW3TYVZ) to understand site usage. Analytics is not loaded until you accept analytics in the consent interface. You may decline analytics or change your choice at any time using “Cookie settings” in the footer.

Your consent choice is stored in your browser's local storage. Embedded forms and third-party content may use their own cookies or similar technologies when they load or when you interact with them.

Hosting and third-party content

The site is hosted using GitHub Pages. Hosting and network providers may process routine technical information, such as IP addresses, request details, browser information, timestamps, and security logs, to deliver and protect the site.

The site also links to or embeds services such as Google Maps, Instagram, Facebook, and other third-party websites. Those services receive information according to their own practices when their content loads or when you follow a link.

Choices and contact

You can decline optional analytics, change your analytics choice through the footer, avoid submitting forms, and choose whether to visit third-party services. Newsletter messages should provide the applicable subscription-management options.

For questions about this policy or information submitted to Slopes to Hope, email drew@slopestohope.com or use the contact page.

This policy may be updated as the website and its services change. The effective date above identifies the current version.
